checks: Exactly three sequential cases select thirteen fixed asset routes, one unknown query route, and one incomplete header; no browser or JavaScript is invoked.
All twelve component source/data files plus manifest/server/design/test are pinned before and after; test artifacts require a new directory.
Ready and terminal PID/token/manifest are joined to the direct owned process and actual 127.0.0.1 port; closed route list is exact.
Normal route responses compare complete original bodies, HTTP200, Content-Length and no-store; exact stop marker must produce normal0, no errors and thirteen successful server request records.

Unknown route must supply no bytes and preserve the declared route error; incomplete header must supply no bytes and preserve the actual http-handler timeout. Both intended refusals require server terminal1 and no stop marker.
All cases retain original stdout/stderr, process identity, return code, time and server records; forced cleanup is a test failure and stops later cases.
Reviewed server source creates no children; direct-child kill is appropriate for this local test. Client socket operations and final collection are separately bounded.
Whole course output and all source subjects are captured in one final ZIP/base64 completion; no automatic repeat or artifact regeneration.
limits: The ten-second case budget is checked between bounded socket operations and applied to terminal communicate; it is not a concurrent hard watchdog. A blocking operation and cleanup can extend observed elapsed time beyond ten seconds.

The test establishes local server source/integrity/refusal behavior only, not native Windows, browser MIME execution, IndexedDB, UI or visual acceptance. HTTP MIME/security headers remain source-reviewed, not newly asserted by this focused three-case test.
execution: No server, test, browser, JavaScript or product execution by reviewer.
